title: Discovering and Alleviating Data Leakage in Staytime Prediction for Live Streaming Recommendation

problem.claim: Multi-window streaming introduces data leakage because short-window training updates embeddings that long-window serving-time prediction cannot access, creating a training–serving mismatch.

gap.claim: Existing live-streaming recommendation methods do not adequately address leakage in multi-window staytime prediction.

contributions.claim: Constructs a benchmark for data leakage detection in live-streaming recommendation.
Identifies shared bottom embeddings as the main source of leakage and identifies a cutoff time where leakage-induced losses outweigh timeliness gains.
Proposes DAST, which decouples embeddings across temporal windows to block leakage paths while preserving multi-window supervision.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments demonstrate consistent improvements on staytime prediction.
The method can be seamlessly integrated into existing frameworks.

narrative_sequence.summary: Staytime prediction is central to live-streaming recommendation.
Prior methods use multi-window streaming to meet live-scenario timeliness requirements.
Multi-window streaming causes data leakage, producing a training–serving mismatch and degrading long-horizon prediction.
The authors introduce a leakage-detection benchmark and locate the main leakage source and cutoff behavior.
DAST decouples temporal-window embeddings and is reported to improve prediction while integrating with existing frameworks.

source_observation.claim: Shared representations across temporal windows can create information paths unavailable at serving time.

interpretation.claim: Training and serving access patterns should be aligned when designing multi-horizon learning systems.

application.claim: Audit shared embeddings for cross-window leakage and consider decoupling representations when serving-time access differs by horizon.

exception.claim: Decoupling may not be necessary when training and serving have equivalent information access or when leakage-induced losses do not outweigh timeliness gains.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify datasets, baseline methods, evaluation metrics, or numerical improvement magnitudes.
The abstract does not describe the benchmark composition or the cutoff-time selection procedure.
The abstract does not report computational costs or limitations.
